title: Fascia traction versus component separation as TAR for the treatment of of complex ventral W3 hernias. A prospective, randomized, multicenter study.
summary:
In patients with ventral W3 hernia, the following procedures should be used to close the abdominal wall:
1. component separation: in this procedure, certain muscle components of the lateral abdominal wall are separated from each other. This allows the three layers of the oblique abdominal musculature can be pulled apart like an accordion, which leads to a significant "stretch gain" and thus to a possible low-tension closure of the large hernia.
2. fascial traction procedure: 
In this procedure, the two straight abdominal muscles and their associated muscle sheaths are pulled along the the edges of the large hernia hole are exposed. Controlled traction  is applied to the abdominal muscles via sutures inserted at the edge of the hernia hole and connected to a special device. The controlled traction is applied over applied for half to three quarters of an hour and also causes low-tension closure of the large hernia gap.
The decision of which procedure the patient receives happens randomly. Similar to a coin toss.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. hernia with a width of 10-20 cm 
2. indication for surgical treatment
3. age of majority
4. consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
1. lack of capacity to consent
2. persons who have been placed in an institution by order of the authorities or the court.
